short_definition: A cryptographic system using the same single secret key for both encryption and decryption.
layman_explanation: A safe that locks and unlocks using the exact same physical key.

short_definition: A cryptographic system using a public key for encryption and a private key for decryption.
layman_explanation: A mailbox where anyone can drop a letter inside using a public slot, but only the owner has the private key to unlock it.

short_definition: A one-way mathematical function that converts input data of any size into a fixed-length string.
layman_explanation: Creating a unique digital fingerprint of a document to verify it hasn't been altered.

short_definition: A method by which one party can prove to another that a statement is true without revealing any secret details.
layman_explanation: Proving you know the combination code to a safe by unlocking it without ever telling anyone what the numbers are.

short_definition: A framework managing digital certificates and public-key encryption to secure communications.
layman_explanation: A global passport office issuing and verifying official digital IDs across the internet.

short_definition: A mathematical scheme demonstrating the authenticity, integrity, and non-repudiation of a digital message.
layman_explanation: A tamper-evident wax seal on a document proving who sent it and that it hasn't been modified.

short_definition: Adding random data to a password before hashing to prevent rainbow table attacks.
layman_explanation: Adding a unique random pinch of salt to every dish so identical passwords produce completely different hash values.

short_definition: A secret value added to passwords before hashing, stored separately from the database.
layman_explanation: An extra secret ingredient kept in a separate safe to protect hashed passwords even if the database leaks.

short_definition: A trusted entity that issues digital certificates validating the identity of entities.
layman_explanation: An official government office issuing passports to verify who people really are.

short_definition: A feature ensuring compromise of a long-term key does not compromise past session keys.
layman_explanation: Changing the locks on your house every 10 minutes so stealing one key doesn't unlock past conversations.

short_definition: A widely used symmetric encryption algorithm utilizing key sizes of 128, 192, or 256 bits.
layman_explanation: The gold-standard cryptographic security lock used by governments and banks worldwide.

short_definition: A pioneer asymmetric cryptosystem based on the practical difficulty of factoring large prime numbers.
layman_explanation: A secure lock mechanism built on mathematical problems that are easy to create but extremely hard to solve without a key.

short_definition: A method allowing two parties to establish a shared secret key over an insecure channel.
layman_explanation: Mixing paint colors publicly in a way that allows two people to end up with the exact same secret color without revealing how to make it.

short_definition: An approach to public-key cryptography based on the algebraic structure of elliptic curves over finite fields.
layman_explanation: A modern encryption method offering strong security with smaller key sizes and lower processing demands.

short_definition: Cryptographic algorithms thought to be secure against attacks by quantum computers.
layman_explanation: Upgrading digital locks today so future super-advanced quantum computers won't be able to pick them.

short_definition: A form of encryption allowing computations to be performed directly on encrypted data without decrypting it first.
layman_explanation: Working on a locked box's contents using robotic gloves without ever unlocking or opening the box.

short_definition: An arbitrary number used along with a secret key for data encryption to ensure distinct ciphertexts.
layman_explanation: A random starting value added to encryption so encrypting the word 'Hello' twice produces completely different outputs.

short_definition: A cryptographic algorithm deriving one or more secret keys from a master value such as a password.
layman_explanation: Stretching a simple user password into a long, complex cryptographic key.

short_definition: An event where two distinct input datasets produce the exact same cryptographic hash output.
layman_explanation: Two completely different people accidentally having identical physical fingerprints.

short_definition: A cryptographic hash function generating a 256-bit (32-byte) signature value for data integrity.
layman_explanation: A reliable cryptographic fingerprinting algorithm used extensively in HTTPS certificates and Bitcoin.

short_definition: An encryption mode where each block of plaintext is XORed with the previous ciphertext block before encryption.
layman_explanation: Linking encrypted data blocks together like a chain so each block depends on the previous one.

short_definition: A arbitrary number used only once in cryptographic communications to prevent replay attacks.
layman_explanation: A single-use tracking number ensuring an attacker cannot resend an old authorized request.

short_definition: A short piece of information used to authenticate a message and confirm data integrity.
layman_explanation: A tamper-evident cryptographic stamp proving a message was written by a trusted sender and not altered.

short_definition: A specific type of message authentication code involving a cryptographic hash function and a secret key.
layman_explanation: Combining a secret password with a document fingerprint to verify authenticity.

short_definition: An arrangement where cryptographic keys are held in safety by a trusted third party.
layman_explanation: Leaving a duplicate master key with a trusted lawyer in case you lose your main key.

short_definition: The administrative tasks involving the generation, exchange, storage, and revocation of cryptographic keys.
layman_explanation: Safely creating, distributing, storing, and destroying physical master keys in an office.

short_definition: A cryptographic key that can be distributed publicly, used to encrypt messages or verify signatures.
layman_explanation: Your public mailing address that anyone can use to send you locked packages.

short_definition: A secret cryptographic key kept strictly confidential, used to decrypt data or generate digital signatures.
layman_explanation: The private key to your personal mailbox that only you possess.

short_definition: The practice of periodically retiring old cryptographic keys and replacing them with new ones.
layman_explanation: Changing office door locks every 6 months so old keys stop working.

short_definition: A precomputed table of hash values used to reverse cryptographic hash functions and crack passwords.
layman_explanation: A massive cheat-sheet of pre-calculated hash values used to look up passwords instantly.

short_definition: Techniques used to make short or weak passwords safer against brute-force attacks by slowing computation.
layman_explanation: Forcing a computer to run a password hashing formula 10,000 times to slow down hackers.

short_definition: A key derivation function applying a pseudorandom function to input passwords alongside a salt value.
layman_explanation: A standard method for turning user passwords into strong encryption keys by repeating hash steps.

short_definition: A password-hashing function incorporating a salt and an adaptable work factor to resist brute-force attacks.
layman_explanation: A password hashing algorithm built to slow down over time as hardware becomes faster.

short_definition: A modern password-hashing algorithm designed to resist GPU-based parallel brute-force attacks.
layman_explanation: An advanced password hashing standard specifically designed to stop high-powered graphics cards from guessing passwords.

short_definition: The practice of concealing a secret message or file within another ordinary message or file.
layman_explanation: Hiding a secret text document inside the invisible pixel data of a digital cat photo.

short_definition: An encryption technique that cannot be cracked if the key is truly random, as long as data and never reused.
layman_explanation: An unbreakable code system using a single-use secret key that is as long as the secret message itself.

short_definition: An encryption algorithm that encrypts data in fixed-size blocks (e.g., 128 bits) at a time.
layman_explanation: Encrypting a long document by chopping it into equal-sized chunks and locking each chunk separately.

short_definition: An encryption algorithm that encrypts data continuous digits or bytes one at a time.
layman_explanation: Encrypting a live video stream byte-by-byte as it flows across the wire.

short_definition: A vulnerability occurring when the same nonce is used multiple times with the same key, leaking data.
layman_explanation: Reusing a single-use key twice, allowing attackers to compare encrypted messages and recover the secret.

short_definition: Intercepting cryptographic handshakes to present fake public certificates to clients.
layman_explanation: Presenting a forged ID card during a handshake to trick users into trusting a secret connection.

short_definition: The unreadable, encrypted output resulting from applying a cryptographic algorithm to plain text.
layman_explanation: The scrambled, illegible string of gibberish produced after locking a document with a password.

short_definition: Unencrypted, human-readable data before it is processed by an encryption algorithm.
layman_explanation: Original readable text before any passwords or encryption locks are applied.

short_definition: The study of analyzing and breaking cryptographic algorithms or ciphers without knowing the key.
layman_explanation: The science of picking cryptographic locks and deciphering coded messages without a key.

short_definition: A measure of randomness or unpredictability collected by an operating system for generating cryptographic keys.
layman_explanation: Using unpredictable real-world randomness (like mouse movements or thermal noise) to generate unbreakable keys.

short_definition: A process by which cryptographic keys are securely negotiated between two parties over a network.
layman_explanation: A set of ground rules allowing two strangers to agree on a secret code over an open telephone line.

short_definition: A decentralized trust model used in PGP where individual users sign each other's public keys.
layman_explanation: Trusting a stranger's identity badge because three of your mutual trusted friends signed off on it.

short_definition: A method for checking the revocation status of X.509 digital certificates efficiently.
layman_explanation: Having a web server present a time-stamped proof from a certificate authority stating 'My badge is still valid today'.

short_definition: An attack exploiting cryptographic error messages regarding invalid padding to decrypt ciphertext.
layman_explanation: Guessing a safe combination by listening to subtle clicking sounds the lock makes when you enter wrong numbers.

short_definition: The capacity of an IT system to quickly switch cryptographic algorithms without major redesign.
layman_explanation: Building a system with modular lock slots so you can swap out old locks for newer ones in minutes.
